question.text: The amount of the heat released when \(20 \mathrm{ml} 0.5 \mathrm{M} \mathrm{NaOH}\) is mixed with \(100 \mathrm{ml} 0.1 \mathrm{M} \mathrm{HCl}\) is \(\mathrm{x} \mathrm{kJ}\). The heat of neutralization is

solution.text:
Hints: \(\underset{20 \times 05}{\mathrm{NaOH}}+\underset{100 \times 01}{\mathrm{HCl}} \rightarrow \mathrm{NaCl}+\underset{10 \text { millimole prodiral }}{\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}}\)
During formation of 10 millimole of \(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\) the heat released is \(\mathrm{xKJ}\). Therefore heat of neutralisation is \(-100 \times \mathrm{KJ} / \mathrm{mol}\) (heat released hence negative)
